SPAN_DERIVATION_MIN.justification: the engine's own span-derivation rule (candidate_diversity.span_derivation_check): ratio < 0.20 = SPAN_UNDERIVED. A MECHANISM_STRENGTHENING mutation must CLEAR this floor — the same rule that gates the grid, not a new one.

EVIDENCE_SUPPORT_MIN.justification: I1's underived flag fires below 0.20; an EVIDENCE_DERIVED_CONSTRAINT mutation must clear the same floor on evidence_support.

DOMAIN_OVERLAP_MIN.justification: REPLAY_CACHE re-adjudication is valid only while the mutated candidate stays in the domain the cached art was found FOR. Guard: >= 1 NON-generic technical term shared between the child's mechanism+intervention and the cached family corpus. ZERO overlap means the mutation abandoned the domain (measured attack: re-adjudicating a cement-curing intervention against battery art fabricates surviving differentiators — false novelty from stale art). The overlap count is RECORDED on every cache adjudication so thin-domain links are auditable. NOTE: entity-term retention vs the problem CANNOT catch this class — entity terms are problem-derived and unchanged by mutations (measured while writing the guard's tests); it is recorded for audit only.

MAX_ITERATIONS_DEFAULT.justification: the CEO minimum loop is DIAGNOSE -> IMPROVE -> RE-EVALUATE -> IMPROVE AGAIN; two iterations demonstrate repeatability at bounded cost

MAX_PROPOSALS_PER_ITERATION.justification: bounded proposal budget: three attempts, then the honest no-defensible-mutation verdict

fields.MECHANISM: The printability of high-performance polymers like polycarbonate is governed by the requirement for a stable running printer that can reach high temperatures, where specific process parameters such as nozzle temperature and extrusion velocity are manipulated to monitor the printer and the process, preventing the delamination observed when thermal stability is insufficient.
fields.INTERVENTION: Implement an open-source hardware upgrade capable of reaching a 200 °C heated bed and 135 °C heated chamber, using open-source firmware by Klipper and Fluidd to control and carefully calibrate the system, ensuring the material remains within the recommended temperature range to manipulate process parameters effectively.
fields.EXPECTED_EFFECT: The thermal gradient between the molten filament and the underlying layer is maintained by the heated chamber and bed, preventing the "layer skipping" failure mode and ensuring high surface quality with no signs of delamination, as evidenced by the production of components with excellent mechanical properties.
fields.FALSIFICATION_TEST: Measure the interlayer adhesion and surface quality of the printed polycarbonate part; if delamination occurs or surface quality is poor despite the 135 °C heated chamber, the hypothesis that this specific thermal configuration prevents layer skipping is false.
fields.MECHANISM_SOURCE_SPAN: The presented design produced a CF-PEEK 3DBenchy and a spiral vase with excellent surface quality and no signs of delamination.
fields.EXPERIMENT: Print a polycarbonate test geometry in an ambient environment above 35C using the open-source hardware upgrade with a 135 °C heated chamber and compare the layer adhesion and surface quality against the baseline control which is printing without a heated chamber at ambient temperature.
fields.EXPERIMENT_BASELINE: printing without a heated chamber at ambient temperature
fields.CONSTRAINT_DERIVED: The heating system must maintain a chamber temperature of 135 °C and a bed temperature of 200 °C to ensure the printer reaches high temperatures stably.
fields.MUTATION_REASON: Repairs the I1_MECHANISM_EVIDENCE_DERIVATION weakness by re-anchoring the mechanism in the verbatim evidence span concerning delamination and surface quality, ensuring the technical vocabulary is derived directly from the cited text.

fields.MECHANISM: High-performance polymer printing, such as polycarbonate, fails due to inadequate thermal management where high nozzle temperatures (up to 500 °C) and heated chambers are required; without stable running printer conditions and continuous monitoring of hardware and firmware, delamination occurs, meaning the mechanism is governed by the need for a heated chamber and calibrated high-temperature operation to prevent surface quality defects and delamination in high-melting-point thermoplastics.
fields.INTERVENTION: Implement the open-source hardware upgrade for low-cost 3D printers, specifically utilizing a heated chamber (135 °C) and heated bed (200 °C) with continuous monitoring via Klipper and Fluidd firmware, to stabilize the process parameters and monitor the printer and process, ensuring the thermal environment compensates for the high baseline thermal energy of polycarbonate.
fields.EXPECTED_EFFECT: The printer produces specimens with excellent surface quality and no signs of delamination, maintaining mechanical integrity (e.g., strength comparable to datasheets or higher) by ensuring the stable running printer reaches and maintains the high temperatures necessary for high-performance polymers, thereby preventing layer skipping caused by thermal shock or inconsistent viscosity.
fields.FALSIFICATION_TEST: If the heated chamber and continuous monitoring are disabled or if the nozzle temperature drops below the required high-temperature range, delamination signs will reappear in the printed polycarbonate specimens, and the measured tensile strength will fall below the 15% outperformance margin in the ZX direction compared to the datasheet.
fields.MECHANISM_SOURCE_SPAN: To print high-performance polymers, a stable running printer that can reach high temperatures is needed.
fields.EXPERIMENT: Print polycarbonate specimens using the open-source hardware upgrade with a heated chamber at 135 °C and continuous monitoring, and compare the surface quality (checking for delamination) and tensile strength against the baseline of printing polycarbonate on an original printer without a heated chamber or continuous monitoring.
fields.EXPERIMENT_BASELINE: original printer without a heated chamber or continuous monitoring
fields.CONSTRAINT_DERIVED: The printer must operate as a stable running printer that can reach high temperatures with a heated chamber to prevent delamination in high-performance polymers.
fields.MUTATION_REASON: Repairs I1_MECHANISM_EVIDENCE_DERIVATION by anchoring the mechanism vocabulary ("stable running printer", "high temperatures", "delamination", "high-performance polymers") directly to the verbatim span from the high-performance polymer 3D printing evidence, ensuring shared content terms exceed the 20% threshold.
